meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the R-601 unit
meta.scope: From the gas packs and the ethanol tank to the cold vent and the product tank T-601, including utilities (instrument air, N₂, chilled water, electrical power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
FIC-201 MFC or its output failing high
controller left in MAN at a high output
set-point entry error
FY-100 ratio set wrong
N1.cons: H₂:CO₂ well above 5; more gas through BPV-601 to the cold vent (larger H₂-rich vent plume); bed temperature rises a few degrees; operation outside the fitted kinetic window

N1.causes:
H₂ pack running down
PR-202 failing closed
XV-201 closing (solenoid or air fault)
MFC failing low
filter F201 plugging
N1.cons: H₂:CO₂ falls, methanol yield falls while the ester route continues; MFC loses its pressure drop before any alarm because PAL-203 is below the 30 bar g reactor pressure; if the supply falls below the reactor, back-flow (see N1.6)

N1.causes:
FT-101 calibration drifting high, so FIC-101 cuts the real CO₂
MFC failing low
PR-102 freezing
N1.cons: H₂:CO₂ above 5 unseen by the operator; yield per CO₂ and the reported conversion are wrong; the FAL/FAH-101 deviation alarms use the same transmitter and cannot see the error

N1.causes: CO₂ pack cold (cylinder cooling during draw-off), pack empty, regulator PR-101 icing
N1.cons: CO₂ flow falls, H₂:CO₂ rises; regulator icing can make the pressure swing; loss of CO₂ trips the unit

N1.dev: Full pack pressure downstream of the regulators
N1.causes: First and second-stage regulator (PR-202, PR-102 or PR-402) failing open or set wrong
N1.cons: MFCs, XVs and tubing see full pack pressure; R-601 pressure rises if the MFC passes; overpressure of components rated for the regulated pressure; H₂ release at a fitting

N1.dev: Back-flow from the reactor into a gas supply
N1.causes:
Supply pressure below the reactor (empty pack with XV open
CO₂ supply drawn down)
MFC open during a pressure test
N1.cons: Reactor gas and ethanol vapour into the CO₂ or N₂ manifold and packs; flammable gas in the CO₂ system; contamination of the pack

N1.dev: N₂ in the feed during operation
N1.causes:
XV-401 or FV-401 passing
FIC-401 left with a set point after start-up
N1.cons: N₂ dilutes the feed, H₂ partial pressure and yield fall slowly; vent rate rises; no safety consequence

N1.dev: Wrong gas connected to a feed line
N1.causes:
Wrong pack or cylinder connected at changeover (air, O₂ or another gas on the H₂ or CO₂ line)
pigtail not purged
N1.cons: Air or O₂ with H₂ over hot reduced Cu catalyst: flammable mixture, fast exotherm, catalyst oxidation, possible explosion in R-601

N1.causes:
N₂ pack running down unnoticed
PR-402 failing closed
N1.cons: The N₂ purge that every trip relies on is not available: H₂ stays in R-601 after a trip; no inert for a shutdown

N1.dev: Impurity in the CO₂ or H₂
N1.causes: Off-specification gas (sulphur or chloride in CO₂, moisture)
N1.cons: Slow poisoning of the Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst; activity and yield fall over days; no immediate hazard

recs.text: Add an absolute high-flow alarm on FT-201 (and FT-101) that works in every controller mode, and an H₂:CO₂ ratio deviation alarm on FY-100.

Raise PAL-203 and PAL-103 above the reactor pressure plus the MFC pressure drop (now 27 bar g, below the 30 bar g reactor), and review PALL-203/103 against the pressure at which the MFCs lose control.
Check FT-101 and FT-201 against a reference meter each campaign and reconcile the CO₂ feed with a GC carbon balance.
Protect the CO₂ pack regulator against cooling and icing (heated or insulated PR-101) and fit a switch-over manifold.
Confirm the pressure rating of the MFCs, XVs and tubing downstream of PR-202, PR-102 and PR-402 against full pack pressure, or add relief valves there (none in 2407-PE-RLB-001).
Put the check valves CK101, CK201, CK301, CK302, CK401 and CK601 in the inspection and proof-test plan.
Add a high alarm on FT-401 while the SIS is in RUN (N₂ passing into the feed).
Use gas-specific pack connections and labels, with a two-person check at every pack change.
Add the N₂ supply (PT-403 above PAL-403) to the start-up permissives, because every trip relies on the N₂ purge.
Check the supplier certificate (sulphur, chloride, moisture) for every CO₂ and H₂ pack received.
Vent-purge the pigtail with N₂ at every pack changeover (written step).
